lens: Rapamycin's lifespan effects reveal a non-monotonic efficacy landscape where dosing kinetics—transient high-dose pulses versus chronic low-level exposure—appear more influential than cumulative mTOR inhibition, challenging conventional gerotherapeutic dosing assumptions.
tensions: Bitto 2016's transient high-dose rapamycin (8 mg/kg/day i.p.) induced ~60% remaining lifespan extension in middle-aged C57BL/6 mice, contrasting with Harrison 2009's chronic low-dose (14 ppm in feed) showing only 14% reduction in 90th-percentile mortality in female UM-HET3 mice.

Miller 2014's dose-response data (42 ppm vs. 14 ppm) indicates greater lifespan extension at higher doses, but the relative efficacy compared to transient regimens remains unquantified across studies.
gaps: Effect of transient rapamycin treatment in female mice is not addressed in the evidence facts.
Direct head-to-head comparison of transient versus chronic dosing regimens in isogenic mouse cohorts.
Integration of healthspan metrics (e.g., cognitive function, frailty) alongside lifespan outcomes for different rapamycin dosing paradigms.

theses.title: The efficacy paradox in rapamycin dosing: transient high-dose interventions surpass chronic regimens in mouse lifespan extension
theses.rationale: Indirect comparisons between Bitto 2016 and Harrison 2009 suggest that short-term, intensive mTOR inhibition may yield greater longevity benefits than lifelong low-dose exposure, highlighting a critical research gap in direct dosing strategy comparisons.

theses.title: Dose-dependent sexual dimorphism in rapamycin's lifespan effects: a meta-analysis of ITP and transient intervention data
theses.rationale: Aggregating data from multiple studies reveals sex-specific responses to rapamycin dosing, with males showing larger extensions in transient studies and females in high-dose chronic studies, informing sex-tailored gerotherapeutic development.
